title: Courts go paperless as e-filing launched
byline: Electronic filing of Court cases has been introduced at the Colombo District Court as part of the island-wide e-Courts Project implemented under the Judicial Service Commission.

title: Solar sector at risk, Chamber of Commerce tells president
byline: The National Chamber of Commerce of Sri Lanka has urged President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to intervene urgently over policy concerns affecting the country’s rooftop solar energy sector, warning that the changes could undermine energy security and economic recovery.

title: Over 53,000 people with kidney disease receive Rs. 10,000 monthly allowance: Minister
byline: As many as 53,604 people suffering from kidney disease are currently receiving a monthly allowance of Rs. 10,000, Minister of Social Security Upali Pannilage told Parliament today.

title: Committee on High Posts approves Ambassador, High Commissioner appointments
byline: The Committee on High Posts of Parliament has approved the appointments of a new Ambassador, a High Commissioner and the Chairman of a state institution.

title: Weather impact to ease as depression weakens
byline: The impact of the deep depression over the Bay of Bengal on Sri Lanka’s weather is expected to gradually decrease from tomorrow (25) as the system weakens into a depression, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Avoid taking painkillers amid rising flu cases: Expert
byline: A surge in Influenza A H1N1 infections is currently being detected in Sri Lanka, with an increase in positive samples identified by the National Influenza Centre at the Medical Research Institute (MRI), Consultant Virologist Dr. Chrishan Jude Jayamaha said.

title: Italian woman falls to death
byline: A young italian woman who fell down the elevated region of the Rawanaella waterfall at a height of more than 100 feet yesterday afternoon died on admission to Demodara hospital.

title: After 22A, NPP Govt to begin work on new Constitution
byline: Despite the Government’s sudden move to enact the 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, which provides for an increase in the retirement age of superior court judges, the introduction of a new Constitution, a key election promise of the ruling National People’s Power (NPP), will come under formal discussion within the party next year, an official said.
